thematic_summaries.title: Divine Prophetic Symbolism
thematic_summaries.summary: God instructs Ezekiel to use dramatic symbolic actions to represent Jerusalem's coming siege and punishment. The prophet's physical demonstrations serve as powerful visual prophecy, communicating God's judgment through embodied metaphor.

thematic_summaries.title: Punishment and Iniquity
thematic_summaries.summary: The chapter reveals God's precise accounting of Israel's generational sins and the consequential punishment. By symbolically bearing the nation's iniquity through restricted movement and rationed food, Ezekiel demonstrates the weight of collective spiritual transgression.

reevaluation.question: How does God's use of prophetic symbolic actions reveal divine communication strategies?
options: Prophetic actions engage multiple sensory experiences

puzzle.question: Imagine you are Ezekiel, tasked to lie on your side to bear the sins of a nation. What does the specific number of days tell you about the weight of the iniquity you must carry?

chain.summary: The LORD shows Ezekiel how the people will eat defiled bread among the nations (v. 13). Leviticus says that those who survive among their enemies will waste away in their iniquity and in the sins of their fathers (Leviticus 26:39).
chain.question: How does Leviticus's warning about wasting away in iniquity help you understand why Ezekiel must bear the iniquity of Israel?

conviction.because: Ezekiel said he had never defiled himself and had never eaten unclean meat from his youth
conviction.template: from today I bring my {feeling:pride, self-righteousness} about {object:my religious habits} into the light and instead of {behavior:judging others' failures}, I will {step:examine my own heart}.
